input.content: Anti-pattern: removing a reader's backward-compatibility fallback branch while a data migration is still in progress. In the "Saved destinations" project, reader.address_of() handled both legacy flat rows ({"address": ...}) and current nested rows ({"destination": {"address": ...}}). A "cleanup" diff deleted the legacy branch, leaving only row["destination"]["address"]. This raises KeyError on any un-migrated row. Because api.list_destinations() maps the reader over ALL records in a list comprehension, a single legacy row breaks the entire read. The README documents a hard contract: "a deployment must read both shapes until migration finishes," "there is no startup migration gate," and data/records.json is a supported MIXED snapshot (legacy + nested rows coexist). migrate_batch() converts only up to `limit` rows per call, so mixed state is the designed, expected state. Lesson for reviewers: a compatibility/fallback branch is removable only AFTER migration is provably complete (telemetry/verification that zero legacy rows remain); until then it is an active-consumer code path, not dead code. Green tests masked this because the only tests used writer.new_destination (nested shape) and never exercised the legacy path.
